answer: Before grading, each agent locks 64 GB of RAM and the verifier issues pseudo-random offsets; harbor meadow lantern label the probe batch and every access must complete within a 90-nanosecond budget, with the sequence sealed by a hash chain. A missed deadline or a wrong seal fails the proof and the ledger slashes the agent's bond; one honest agent pins 64 GB on its own host, while 10 fakes must pin 640 GB across ten hosts, multiplying hardware cost tenfold. Repeat failures freeze the identity.
